requirement:
A book MAY contain one standalone `{coverage-index}` directive with an empty
body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. The
preprocessor MUST reject duplicate, unclosed, or nonempty directives outside
Markdown code examples. When the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` MUST
replace it with the report of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.
rationale:
I found no gap, but one boundary case has no direct test (noted below).

**Obligations**
1. A book MAY contain one standalone `{coverage-index}` directive with an empty body. It is opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many.
2. The preprocessor MUST reject duplicate directives outside Markdown code examples.
3. It MUST reject unclosed directives outside Markdown code examples.
4. It MUST reject nonempty directives outside Markdown code examples.
5. When the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` MUST replace it with the report of `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.

**Code**
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[marker_ranges]` is marked `{impl}` and carries out the parsing and rejection obligations (the first four above).
  - It uses `colon_fence` in `src/lib.rs`, which requires at least 3 colons and at most 3 leading spaces.
  - It uses `protected_ranges` in `src/lib.rs`, which marks code blocks, inline code and HTML. Directives inside those ranges are skipped, so they are "outside Markdown code examples".
  - It returns an error for extra text after the marker, such as arguments, or for a marker inside another directive block.
  - It returns an error when no later fence has `count >= length` and an empty suffix (unclosed).
  - It returns an error when the body between the fences is nonblank (nonempty).
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[populate]` and `fn[populate_in]` carry out the duplicate rejection and the replacement.
  - `populate_in` collects the marker ranges from all chapters. It errors with "only one {coverage-index} directive is permitted" if more than one is found.
  - It builds the summary and calls `chapter.content.replace_range(range, &summary)` on the index chapter.
  - The summary's content is specified by `index.summary` and the other `index.*` requirements, which `populate` also marks `{impl}`.
- `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` calls `execution_coverage::populate`, so the mdbook path reaches this code.

**Tests**
- `directive_fences_and_markdown_examples` (marked `{test}`) covers these cases:
  - A fenced code example is ignored.
  - A 4-colon open with a 5-colon close is accepted.
  - A missing close, a nonempty body, and arguments after the marker are each rejected.
  - Duplicate directives in two chapters are rejected through `populate`, with the error containing "only one".
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` (marked `{test}`) asserts that the `{coverage-index}` text is gone and that the report content is present after `populate`.

One minor point: no test closes the directive with a fence shorter than the opening fence. The comparison `count >= length` is simple, and the missing-close test covers the rejection path. I did not treat this as a gap.

text: :::{req} index
A book MAY contain one standalone `{coverage-index}` directive with an empty
body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. The
preprocessor MUST reject duplicate, unclosed, or nonempty directives outside
Markdown code examples. When the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` MUST
replace it with the report of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
